Programme: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound
Institution: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (IE) · Universidade Lusófona (PT) · Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre / LMTA (LT)
City: Dublin (Dún Laoghaire, sem 1) → Lisbon (sem 2) → Vilnius (sem 3) → sem 4 thesis at IADT, Lusófona or LMTA (student selects host)
Degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master — joint diploma supplement 'MA in Sound (ReSound)' PLUS multiple degrees: IADT 'Master of Arts in Sound', Lusófona 'Master's in Sound Production Technology', LMTA 'Master of Arts in Film'
Type: Consortium within the FilmEU European University alliance: art-and-technology institute (IADT, hosts Ireland's National Film School), private university film school (Lusófona), state academy of music and theatre (LMTA)
Focus: Sound Design · Film/Game Sound · Immersive Audio · Music Production · Electronic Music · Sonic Arts
Language: English (all instruction)
Duration/ECTS: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS — CONFIRMED by summing the published module table (30 ECTS per semester; sem 4 = 30 ECTS Thesis). Programme runs early September to early June of year 2.
Tuition (intl): €15,000 total for the whole 4-semester programme for non-scholarship holders, paid €7,500 before semester 1 and €7,500 before semester 3. Identical for EU and non-EU. Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders pay nothing. Fee covers all classes, insurance, enrolment at each partner, examinations and the final diploma; it does NOT cover travel, visas, accommodation or living costs. Living costs estimated at €600–1,000 per month.
Funding: Full (for Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders) / self-pay fallback €15,000 total
Scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Scholarship, "awarded on the basis of excellence" — open to any nationality including Tunisian; eligibility is holding a first higher-education degree or recognised equivalent, and not already having held an EMJM/Erasmus Mundus scholarship. "A maximum of 24 places are offered at ReSound each year. An Erasmus Mundus scholarship will be available only to a percentage of those places." CORRECTION: the site says "only to a percentage", not "a significant percentage".
Stipend: €1,400 per month. Scholarship holders "pay no tuition fees and receive a scholarship of 1,400 EUR per month. These Erasmus+ scholarships contribute to travel, visa and a living allowance." Note: the scholarship does not begin until the student has arrived in Dublin and registered — he must fund his own travel to Ireland. Additional Erasmus Mundus special-needs funding exists for documented long-term impairments.
Accepts non-music?: Yes — the strongest wording in this batch. "ReSound is open to both European and non-European students who hold a bachelor's degree in sound, music, film, or media studies. Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies." FAQ: "I have not formally studied sound. Is prior experience in sound a requirement for admission? It is not a requirement to have formally studied sound specifically." CORRECTION to the draft: the current published eligibility text does NOT name "computational science" as an accepted field — the accepted list is sound, music, film, media studies, plus the other-fields-with-relevant-experience clause. A software-engineering BSc therefore goes through the discretionary clause and needs demonstrable sound/music practice, which his DJ/producer work can supply.
Portfolio spec: "Portfolio of previous sound/media related work. Please include a short reflective paragraph on each piece explicitly stating your role in the work. Please supply no more than 3 examples. You can supply a single hyperlink to a portfolio website or a compilation audio or video file. The team can realistically listen/watch 10-15 minutes of material per application, so please select the best work." FAQ adds: works can be "audio recordings or audio related outputs... video related outputs and there could be songs, music, soundtracks, arts and Electro acoustic music performance"; "Focus on contrast rather than have three of the same sort of style"; and explicitly "If I do not already have a suitable portfolio of work can I create one specifically for this programme? Yes. Absolutely."
Audition: No live audition and no on-site test. There IS an online interview stage: "Applicants with the highest scores resulting from the application package, which includes the Portfolio, will be called for an online Interview." FAQ: "Interviews are scheduled to take place online (over Microsoft Teams) during March", with at least one week's notice. English skills are judged partly from the interview. Offers expected no later than end of April.
Entry requirements: Bachelor's degree in sound, music, film or media studies (minimum EQF Level 6 or equivalent; NARIC Ireland used to check equivalence). Other fields considered with relevant prior experience. Also required: passport copy, headshot, stamped degree documents + transcripts (certified English translation if needed), CV of professional qualifications and experience, TWO letters of recommendation (at least one academic, addressed to 'board members of ReSound'), letter of motivation (max 1000 characters, explicitly 'do not use AI / Large Language Models'), a 500-character description of a proposed final thesis project, portfolio, English proof. English: IELTS 6.0 with no component below 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 79 / Duolingo 110 / Cambridge B2 / LanguageCert ESOL, taken within the last two years; OR a full EQF Level 4+ qualification of at least one academic year taught through English. Final-year undergraduates may apply (conditional offer). No age limit and no time limit on when the bachelor was obtained.
What you study: Curriculum built on three pillars (Societal, Skills, Creative). Sem 1 IADT: Acoustics & Psychoacoustics (5), Audio and Music Production (10 — studio procedure, microphone technique, signal flow, critical listening), Synthesis and Sampling (5 — analogue/digital synthesis rebuilt in open-source environments), Interactive Systems (5), Sound Psychology (5). Sem 2 Lusófona: Film Sound Theory (5), Interdisciplinary Project Incubation (5), Sound Ecosystems (5), Sound/Music Interface (5 — music fundamentals bridged to electroacoustic music, soundscape composition, field recording, digital synthesis), Film Audio: Post-production Tools (10 — Pro Tools, includes Avid 101 and 110 certification). Sem 3 LMTA: Sound and the Environment (5), Film Sound: Integrative Methods and Practice (10), Sound Concepts (5), Sound Design and Immersion (5 — immersive mixing), Thesis Preparation (5). Sem 4: practice-based Thesis (30).
Facilities: CONFIRMED per campus. IADT: National Film School, two Dolby Atmos mix suites, a 5.1 surround mixing suite, Foley recording stage, vocal booth, immersive media production facility (VR/AR), two radio studios. Lusófona: general-purpose recording studio, 5.1 Dolby Surround post room, 7.1.4 Dolby Atmos post auditorium, Sonic Arts Lab (audio+video+microcontrollers), Apple/MIDI-equipped labs, large equipment loan warehouse. LMTA: spatial sound sphere, two recording studios, video/audio editing workstations, 99-seat cinema hall, dedicated sound mixing and mastering cinema hall, two film studios.

Deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. FAQ (still live): the 2026 application period "will close at 17:00 (Western European Time) on the 20th January 2026"; the application page now reads "Applications for ReSound 2026 have now closed." (The draft's claim of an extension to 27 January 2026 could NOT be confirmed anywhere on the site.) No 2027 call published as of July 2026.

Main obstacles: only 24 places worldwide and only a percentage funded; the centre of gravity is sound design / film / immersive rather than club music, so his three portfolio pieces should be contrasting (at least one designed or narrative piece, not three dance tracks); and he must sit IELTS/TOEFL and secure two references, one academic.

Honest framing for him: this is audio ENGINEERING and interaction design — spatial audio, VR/AR sound, AI for sound, new interfaces for musical expression — not beat-making, mixing records or DJ craft.

Programme: Teilzeit-Master Audio Experience Design
Institution: Staatliche Hochschule für Musik Trossingen
City: Trossingen, Baden-Württemberg (small town, approx. 78647; nearest larger centre Tuttlingen)
Type: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
Focus: Sound Design / Audio UX and design research; immersive and spatial sound. Explicitly NOT music production.
Language: German — all programme material is German, and the school's binding Immatrikulationssatzung requires German B2 for foreign applicants. Crucial nuance, confirmed verbatim: for bachelor's and master's programmes generally (Gymnasiallehramt, Musikpädagogik and Musikwissenschaft excepted), the B2 certificate must be produced 'vor Ablauf der Rückmeldefrist für das dritte Fachsemester' — i.e. by the re-registration deadline for the THIRD semester, not at application. So he could be admitted and start without B2 and certify it during year one; re-registration into semester three is impossible without it.
Duration/ECTS: 4 semesters (Regelstudienzeit), part-time at 50% workload / 60 ECTS total (15 ECTS per semester) — CONFIRMED in the page's 'Facts' box. Max 10 on-site days per semester; supervision otherwise mainly remote.
Tuition (intl): SELF-PAY, now CONFIRMED — this is the biggest correction. The programme page's 'Keine Studiengebühren für EU-Bürger:innen bei Erstmaster' does not help him. Baden-Württemberg's LHGebG applies: 'Studiengebühr Internationale Studierende: 1.500 € pro Semester gem. § 3ff LHGebG für Studierende aus Ländern außerhalb der EU / des EWR ohne inländische Hochschulzulassungsberechtigung ... für alle Bachelor- und konsekutiven Master-Studiengänge'. Over four semesters that is €6,000, plus Verwaltungskostenbeitrag €80.00 and Studierendenwerksbeitrag €58.60 per semester (as of May 2026) — about €6,554 total. Exemptions exist under §§5–7 LHGebG (e.g. permanent domestic residence, spouses/children of EU/EEA nationals) and a waiver 'aufgrund besonderer Begabung gemäß § 6 Abs. 4 LHGebG' is possible on application; waiver applications are due 21 January / 21 June for the following semester.
Funding: None realistically (non-EU fee of €1,500/semester confirmed; no institutional support)
Scholarship: None from the institution — stated plainly on the school's own page for international applicants: 'Die Trossinger Hochschule kann keine finanzielle Unterstützung leisten', with only small Förderverein grants (e.g. competition travel) on application. It adds that German partial scholarships from the ministry or DAAD 'können erst nach einigen Semestern erfolgreichen Studierens beantragt werden' and go to very few students. A special-talent tuition waiver under § 6 Abs. 4 LHGebG is the one real lever. DAAD study scholarships normally require full-time enrolment, which a 50% part-time master does not satisfy — treat DAAD as unavailable here unless DAAD confirms otherwise.
Stipend: None. No stipend exists for this programme, and the school states it cannot provide financial support.
Accepts non-music?: Yes — explicitly, and computer science is named. The official page opens with: 'Ob in Architektur, Design, Musik, Medien, Informatik, Pädagogik oder Wissenschaft: hier verbindest du dein bisheriges Fachgebiet mit auditiven Perspektiven' ('Whether in architecture, design, music, media, COMPUTER SCIENCE, education or science: here you connect your existing field with auditory perspectives'), and lists 'Einstieg aus vielen Bereichen und Disziplinen möglich'. A software-engineering BSc is squarely in scope, and the assessment is of the idea, not of musicianship: 'Wir bewerten das Potenzial deiner Idee.'
Portfolio spec: EXACT, confirmed verbatim, and note the delivery mechanism. In the portal, where a 'Link für die erste Phase' is requested, you literally enter 'USB-Stick' and then POST a USB stick containing: (1) the exposé of the project idea — 'Kurzes (Selfie-)Vorstellungsvideo zum Vorhaben (max. 2 Minuten)', a written account of 'max. 3 Seiten', and any early media sketches; (2) 'Eine Auswahl deiner bisherigen Arbeiten (max. 7)' — up to SEVEN previous works showing the full breadth of his output, each described in 'max. 1/2 Seite pro Arbeit', stating the year of creation, the idea/concept behind it, how it was realised, and the team involved if any. Separately uploaded via the portal's upload button: motivation letter, certificates, Zulassungsantrag, payment confirmation.
Audition: No on-site entrance examination — 'Es gibt keine Aufnahmeprüfung in Präsenz.' Shortlisted applicants get 'ein kurzes Gespräch per Videochat (ca. 15 Minuten)'. Note: separately, applicants without a German Abitur may face a Begabtenprüfung (a two-hour handwritten essay in German plus a 10–15 minute oral exam in German) — that route is described for applicants lacking a higher-education entrance qualification, so it should not apply to a completed BSc, but confirm.
Entry requirements: No specific bachelor subject is mandated. The page invites entrants from 'Architektur, Design, Musik, Medien, Informatik, Pädagogik oder Wissenschaft' and lists 'Einstieg aus vielen Bereichen und Disziplinen möglich' as a selling point. Submit: a motivation letter with a chronological account of prior musical and/or design background plus any publications or competition results; certificates (Zeugnisse); the Zulassungsantrag; proof of the transfer (fee payment); further documents per the Zulassungsantrag; and the media materials described below. German B2 per the Immatrikulationssatzung, deferrable to the third-semester re-registration deadline. The legally binding text is the Immatrikulationssatzung.
What you study: CONFIRMED on the official page: 'Development of audio experiences at the intersections of music, sound, language, technology, design, user experience and design research.' Semesters 1–2 centre on the applicant's own project, supported by design-research seminars, individual supervision (mostly remote) and up to four subject-specific workshops per semester with external experts, plus one smaller interdisciplinary project with students from the other part-time masters. From semester 3 the master's project takes over (it may but need not build on the first-year work). The page is unusually blunt about what this is not: 'This is not music production. Bei Audio Experience Design gestaltest du Klang als Erfahrung, nicht nur Tracks.' and, as a tagline, 'Stop producing. Start designing. Sound ist Material. Sound ist UX'. New programme, first intake October 2026, up to 10 students per year.
Facilities: Not published for this programme. The school has a Tonstudio and a 'Digital Concert Space', and links a Modulhandbuch and Studienverlaufsplan, but no studio, console or immersive-room inventory is given on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. With max 10 on-site days per semester, physical facility access would in any case be limited.
Opens: 1 March (the school's standing application window for the winter semester is 01.03.–01.04.; for the summer semester 01.10.–01.11., but this programme has a winter start only).
Deadline: 1 March to 1 April, a standing annual window for the winter-semester intake — confirmed both on the programme page ('Vom 1. März bis 1. April reichst du deine Bewerbung über das Bewerbungsportal ein') and on the school's general Bewerbung page ('01.03. bis 01.04. für das Wintersemester'). The programme itself launches in October 2026; for an October 2027 start the window should be 1 March – 1 April 2027 — confirm when the portal opens (today is July 2026).
Fit notes: The entry process is the friendliest anywhere in this batch — computer science named as a welcome background, no on-site exam, a 15-minute video interview, up to seven free-form works, and a German requirement he can defer to his second year. But almost everything after entry works against him. The school itself says 'This is not music production' and 'Stop producing. Start designing' — the deliverable is audio UX and design research, not tracks. It is 50% part-time and only 60 ECTS, which is a serious problem for a Tunisian national: German study visas and residence permits are premised on full-time study, so the part-time structure puts the whole immigration basis in doubt and should be checked with the German embassy before anything else. As a non-EU student he pays €1,500 per semester (about €6,554 all-in over two years) with no institutional funding and DAAD effectively off the table. And Trossingen is a village in rural Baden-Württemberg, roughly the opposite of a DJ's environment. Pursue only if he genuinely wants to become a sound designer for interfaces, installations and spatial experiences — and only after the visa question is answered.

Programme: Diplôme de La Fémis — Département SON (Concours international, reserved for non-EEA nationals)
Institution: La Fémis — École nationale supérieure des métiers de l'image et du son
Degree: Diplôme de La Fémis conférant le grade de Master
Type: Public national film school (Ministère de la Culture / CNC)
Focus: Film Sound (production sound, editing, mixing, sound design for cinema)
Language: French only — CONFIRMED verbatim: 'La maîtrise de la langue française est obligatoire. Les épreuves se déroulent en français, de même que les enseignements dispensés à l'École.'
Duration/ECTS: 4 years full-time (cursus principal, all seven departments of the concours général and concours international). ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED.
Tuition (intl): CONFIRMED verbatim: 'Le montant des frais de scolarité pour les candidats étrangers hors Union Européenne ayant réussi les épreuves d'admission à La Fémis s'élève à 32000 euros au total pour les quatre ans de scolarité' — paid as 'Des frais de scolarité d'un montant de 8000 euros (à renouveler chaque année)' by bank transfer. Concours registration fee €142, card only, non-refundable (waived for holders of a French CROUS bourse). CVEC ~€105 at the 2025 rate. A sworn declaration undertaking to pay the €8,000 must be sent before Fri 24 April 2026 as a financial guarantee; admitted candidates must supply, before Fri 3 July 2026, an attestation covering the full four years, 'qui pourra notamment être délivrée par l'Ambassade de France pour les bénéficiaires d'une bourse ou d'un soutien financier'. Living costs excluded.
Funding: None from the school for non-EU candidates — a self-pay route unless a third party funds it: 'Les candidats peuvent assumer cette charge financière ou elle peut être assurée pour leur compte par un tiers (ambassade, famille, entreprise privée…).'
Scholarship: None found from La Fémis for international-concours students. The modalités explicitly point to an Ambassade de France attestation for scholarship holders, so a French Embassy / Campus France Tunisie bourse is the only realistic vehicle. 'Pour les étudiants en situation de difficulté, les bourses et aides sociales permettent de les accompagner pendant leurs études' — general hardship aid, not an entry scholarship.
Stipend: None. €32,000 total tuition plus four years of Paris living costs must be covered by the candidate or a sponsor.
Accepts non-music?: YES for the formal diploma requirement — CONFIRMED. Only 'l'équivalent d'un baccalauréat' plus two successive years of higher education in ANY field is required, and the professional route accepts two years of work experience 'quel que soit le secteur d'activité'. No music or audio qualification is demanded, and the science half of the son written paper suits an engineering graduate. BUT the same paper tests cinema culture, sound aesthetics AND musical culture, and the whole concours is cinema-centred — the barrier is cultural and linguistic, not formal.
Portfolio spec: CONFIRMED, 2026 cycle. Four documents uploaded via the candidate space by Thu 12 Feb 2026 12:00, all strictly anonymous (no name in the dossier, audio/video files or credits, on pain of exclusion): (1) 'dossier personnel d'enquête' on one of three imposed themes, max 20 pages — written part max 10 pages (font ≥10, numbered) + visual part max 10 pages, optionally illustrated by a video document max 5 min AND/OR a sound document max 5 min (links on page 1 via an anonymous account); a dossier that does not treat the chosen theme, or treats it as fiction, is not marked and eliminates the candidate; (2) 'note de synthèse' max 1 A4 page; (3) 'lettre de présentation et motivation' max 1 A4 page; (4) 'un portfolio de projets personnels : 3 projets au maximum, sur 8 pages au maximum, au format PDF' — accepted: photos, drawings, screenplay, comics, video (viewing link in the PDF), 'son (via un lien d'écoute indiqué sur le PDF)'; total moving-image or sound running time limited to 3 minutes.
Audition: CONFIRMED. FIRST ROUND, remote by videoconference: film-analysis test (Wed 25 Feb 2026 10:00, 3 hours; extract screened 3 times; candidate records a 5-8 minute spoken analysis; coefficient 1) and DEPARTMENTAL SON tests (24-26 Feb 2026, coefficient 2) — (a) written paper 1h30 on cinema culture, sound aesthetics, musical culture and the science syllabus; (b) oral 30 min: 'Les jurés pourront revenir sur l'épreuve écrite, et interrogeront le ou la candidat·e sur son parcours et ses motivations.' '14 candidats, au maximum, sont déclarés admissibles.' SECOND ROUND: a single public oral interview IN PARIS, max 30 min, coefficient 4, between Mon 15 and Fri 26 June 2026, covering culture, tastes, experience and projects, the earlier tests, and the note de synthèse / motivation letter / portfolio. 'À l'issue de l'épreuve, 7 candidats au maximum peuvent être déclarés admis (ou sur liste d'attente) le jury ayant pris en compte l'équilibre des départements' — 7 places TOTAL across all seven departments.
Entry requirements: CONFIRMED. Nationality: the concours international is open ONLY to nationals of countries outside the EEA, Andorra, Monaco and Switzerland — correct route for a Tunisian; dual nationals of those states must take the concours général. Age: 'Les candidats doivent être âgés de moins de 27 ans au 1er janvier 2026.' Diploma: equivalent of a baccalauréat AND at least two successive validated years of higher education (by equivalence), with certified translations. Alternative 'professionnel' route: under 30 at 1 January, baccalauréat, and at least two years of professional activity 'quel que soit le secteur d'activité'. French: for non-nationals of francophone states, a certificate from a French-government-approved body attesting CEFR B1 minimum, or a higher-education diploma obtained in a francophone cursus. Maximum three attempts across all Fémis concours. AI use is strictly forbidden: 'L'usage de l'I.A. est strictement interdit.'
What you study: Four-year cinema cursus in the Son department alongside the six other departments (réalisation, scénario, image, montage, décor, production), built around collective film productions. A detailed module list is not published in the concours modalités — UNVERIFIED. The written test syllabus signals the content: cinema culture (films, professions, equipment), 'esthétique sonore et culture musicale', and applied science — powers/roots/logarithms, acoustic units, periodic and sinusoidal motion, Fourier's law, production and propagation of sound (reflection, absorption, diffusion, focusing, refraction, diffraction), microphones/amplifiers/loudspeakers, oscillating circuits, impedance, hearing and loudness (Fechner's law, Bel/Decibel/Phone, Fletcher diagram), DC/AC and Ohm's law. The document adds: 'C'est uniquement la « compréhension », le « principe » des notions énumérées ci-dessus, qui sont pris en compte.'
Facilities: France's flagship national film school; the Son department works inside full-scale collective film productions with réalisation, image, montage and production. Detailed studio inventory and alumni lists not in the concours document — UNVERIFIED. Confirmed warning: 'L'enseignement à La Fémis est à plein temps et requiert l'assiduité des étudiants. Un travail en parallèle est donc possible mais seulement les week-ends ou soirées.'

Programme: Master Cinéma et audiovisuel — parcours Son (entered via the Master 1 Cinéma & Audiovisuel Parcours Généraliste, then Master 2 Son)
Institution: Université Toulouse - Jean Jaurès / École Nationale Supérieure d'AudioVisuel (ENSAV)
Type: Public university film school — école interne of Université Toulouse - Jean Jaurès, described as the first and only national film school located outside Paris
Focus: Film Sound + Sound Design + Recording, practice-based and very production-heavy. This is cinema and audiovisual sound, not music production.
Language: French throughout
Duration/ECTS: 2 years. M1 entry requires Bac+3 / 180 ECTS; M2 Son entry requires Bac+4 / 240 ECTS. Programme ECTS total not published — UNVERIFIED (French masters are 120 ECTS).
Tuition (intl): Public university fees, but the exemption position has worsened. The non-EU differentiated master rate for 2026-2027 is €3,950/yr nationally. Université Toulouse Jean Jaurès's own exemption policy was not read and is UNVERIFIED, but décret n° 2026-385 of 19 May 2026 abolished blanket institutional exemptions across the whole French public system and caps discretionary exemptions at 30% of affected students in 2026-2027 and 25% in 2027-2028. Budget €3,950/yr plus CVEC (~€105) and verify with ENSAV/UT2J directly.
Funding: None to partial — discretionary and capped fee exemption only, no stipend.
Scholarship: None programme-specific. External routes only: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated, €1,181/month at master level, age cap 25, national Campus France deadline in early January with institutional internal deadlines in the preceding autumn), Campus France Tunisie and French Embassy bourses, and BGF which brings full fee exemption.
Accepts non-music?: YES for the M1 entry point, and this remains the most explicitly CS-friendly admissions wording found in France: the accepted bachelor list names 'DE L'INFORMATIQUE' outright, so a Bac+3 in computer science is a named, accepted qualification for the Master 1 Généraliste. No music degree, no audition and no music-theory test. BUT — and this is the correction — that acceptance gets him into the GENERALIST M1, not into Son. M2 Son requires Bac+4 and presumes sound training already acquired during ENSAV's own Licence and M1 years, so reaching the Son specialisation means completing the generalist M1 first and then competing internally.
Portfolio spec: Not published. The application is a downloadable ENSAV dossier form emailed back to the school. For the Production parcours the dossier requires a one-page mémoire project; the equivalent creative requirement for the generalist M1 and for M2 Son — number of works, length, format — is NOT specified on any public page. UNVERIFIED. He must request the current dossier from ensav@univ-tlse2.fr.
Audition: No live audition and no written concours found. Selection is on dossier, with a possible interview after the file review ('un entretien peut être programmé'). Whether the interview is remote or on-site in Toulouse is UNVERIFIED.
Entry requirements: IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL CORRECTION. ENSAV does not run a 'parcours Son' from M1. It runs a Master 1 Cinéma & Audiovisuel Parcours Généraliste (alongside M1 Production, REX and XR), and Son is one of seven M2 specialisations (Son, Image, Réalisation, Production, REX, Architecture Décor/VFX, XR). M1 Généraliste entry: 'Licence Création Audiovisuelle ou d'une formation bac+3 équivalente dans les domaines des arts, des arts du spectacle, de l'architecture, du design, des arts plastiques, DE L'INFORMATIQUE ou des beaux-arts', i.e. Bac+3 / 180 ECTS. M2 Son entry: Bac+4 / 240 ECTS, and the ENSAV page states that entrants must have 'already been previously trained in sound basics during the generalist years of Licence and Master 1' at ENSAV. Selection is on dossier, and after the file review 'un entretien peut être programmé avec le candidat'. Dossiers are emailed directly to ensav@univ-tlse2.fr — the Son route is handled by ENSAV itself, not via Mon Master (the Production parcours does use Mon Master). Extra-European applicants are also routed through Études en France. Contact: Djazaira Berkouk, ensav@univ-tlse2.fr, 05 61 50 44 46; ENSAV, 56 rue du Taur, 31000 Toulouse, 05 61 50 35 07.
What you study: Roughly 15 compulsory exercises across the two years — sound pieces, documentaries and fiction works, each with defined pedagogical constraints — plus a personal film at the end of M1 and of M2 with no restriction on genre or duration, each accompanied by a methodological dissertation. Taught content covers acoustic principles, analogue and digital audio technology, sound recording, editing, mixing and diffusion. CONFIRMED M2 Son exercises specifically: location sound recording (phonography), documentary sound creation, sound post-production, a written audio-technology dissertation, sound design for a visual sequence, collaborative work with the Image and Réalisation M2 students on the 'Filmer le Travail' project, and a final thesis with an accompanying audio or audiovisual product defended before a professional jury.
Facilities: ENSAV is a public national film school with seven M2 specialisations co-located, so sound students work inside real crews with image, directing, production, VFX and XR students. The M2 Son year emphasises analogue and digital audio technology, acoustic principles and professional audio systems, and includes a cross-specialisation collaborative project. Language: Greek, with some parts in English — VERIFIED verbatim: "Η γλώσσα διδασκαλίας είναι η ελληνική, με κάποια μέρη της διδασκαλίας να πραγματοποιούνται και στην αγγλική." The thesis may be written in English. There is no English-taught track.

Stipend: None. Accepts non-music?: Yes, explicitly. Πληροφορικής (Informatics), Ηλεκτρονικής, Ηλεκτρολογίας, Φυσικής and Polytechnic-school engineering diplomas are all on the named eligible list, so a software-engineering BSc is squarely eligible without invoking the escape clause. The practical gate is not the discipline but DOATAP equivalence recognition of the Tunisian degree.

No number of works, duration or format is prescribed. But it is decisive in practice: Article 11 of the regulation sets a 100-point scale of formal qualifications 30, scientific/artistic qualifications 30, written examinations where held 15, and statement of purpose plus interview 25 — so 30 of 100 points hang on demonstrable artistic or research output, and a further sub-rule gives up to 10 points for certified professional experience at 2 points per year, which he does not have.

Entry requirements: Holders of a first-cycle degree from a Greek HEI or an equivalent foreign institution under Article 34 of Law 4485/2017, in a field related to (a) sound and music art and science, (b) SOUND TECHNOLOGY — explicitly including Μουσικής Τεχνολογίας & Ακουστικής, Φυσικής, ΠΛΗΡΟΦΟΡΙΚΗΣ (Informatics), Ηλεκτρονικής, Ηλεκτρολογίας, Τεχνολογίας Ήχου and engineering diploma-holders from Polytechnic or Architecture schools, or (c) applied fields such as cultural management, cultural technology and communication, cinema and mass media. Required documents: application form stating the chosen specialisation; ID copy; two photographs; degree certificates — and for foreign degrees, "συνοδευόμενους από βεβαίωση αναγνώρισης ισοτιμίας από τον Δ.Ο.Α.Τ.Α.Π.", i.e. a formal DOATAP equivalence recognition, which is a slow and non-trivial process for a Tunisian degree; a certificate of at least good knowledge of English; full CV; statement of purpose; and AT LEAST TWO recommendation letters. Duration/ECTS: 1 year full-time, structured as "3 study blocks, each of 12 weeks". Credits/ECTS NOT PUBLISHED — still UNVERIFIED (a one-year UK MA is normally 180 UK credits / 90 ECTS, but the page does not say so).

UK residents may be eligible for a postgraduate tuition fee loan." Genuinely cheap for a UK MA and well below ICMP/ACM/BIMM. Our scholarships are reviewed yearly, with applications generally opening 3-6 months prior to the course starting. Scholarship awards generally cover the cost of all course tuition fees." The fact box adds: "Scholarships available: Scholarship awards available in Brighton and Sheffield." Full-tuition awards are unusually generous for a private college — and unreachable on this course from Tunisia.

Accepts non-music?: Partly. The wording is "an undergraduate honours degree in a RELEVANT subject area", which a software-engineering BSc is not, but the page immediately softens this: "The MA is focused on your own work and experience. That means you don't necessarily need an undergraduate degree to study this MA if you already have the right amount of professional experience", plus the APEL route. In practice a strong portfolio and demonstrable music activity would carry the application. Academic anyway, given the residency bar.
Portfolio spec: No portfolio specification is published. Admission is assessed conversationally: "We consider all applications on their own merit and potential. We'll invite you to a 1-1 session, either in person or by video conference."
Audition: NO AUDITION. A one-to-one session, "either in person or by video conference", in which "you'll have the opportunity to find out all about WaterBear and talk about your interests, achievements and career goals." One of the most accessible admissions processes in this slice — which makes the residency bar all the more annoying.
Entry requirements: Verbatim: "Typically, you'll have an undergraduate honours degree in a relevant subject area and a clear interest in your subject. If you don't have an honours degree, you may be able to satisfy entry requirements through the Accreditation of Prior Experiential Learning (APEL) process. This provides an entry route for those who have a significant amount of music industry-relevant experience but may not have a degree." The fact box summarises it as "An undergraduate degree or via accreditation of prior learning". English: "If English isn't your first language, you'll need to achieve an equivalent to the IELTS Academic 6.5 overall score, a minimum of 5.5 in Reading, Writing and Listening, and a minimum of 6.0 in Speaking" — the 5.5 floor in three of four skills is more forgiving than most UK master's.
What you study: Three 12-week blocks combining performance, production and business, delivered through "Lectures, seminars, tutorials and workshops; One-to-one mentoring; Assignments, assessments and feedback sessions; Masterclasses; Special events and conferences; Performances and gigs; Peer collaboration; Networking and social events", with free studio time to make a record and work across Pro Tools, Ableton and Logic Pro. Framed around three strands: "Your music: You will create and craft your music to record and mix in professional studios", "Your business: You will understand your brand, product and market", "Your career".
Facilities: Strong and confirmed at college level: Hanover House, Brighton (four floors, a 1,000 sq ft recording studio with analogue and digital gear, instrument rooms, Mac suites); Sheffield in the former Gatecrasher building (live room, recording suite, Mac suites); partner studios including Brighton Electric, and in Sheffield Spring Tank, Tecna, Hybrid3 and MU Studios; WaterBear's own two Brighton venues giving students bookable gig space. On this course specifically: "The MA Music Performance, Production and Business course also includes free time in professional recording studios, working with producers and engineers to make a record", plus masterclasses, songwriting camps, industry showcases, festivals and conferences.
Opens: UNVERIFIED. Applications are made directly via WaterBear's "Apply Now" route. Scholarship applications "generally open 3-6 months prior to the course starting", so for a September 2027 start expect scholarship applications around March-June 2027.
Deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No application deadline is published. The only published date is the next intake: "Start date: September 2026". Nothing for 2027 yet.

This course is not available for students located outside of the UK." The fact box repeats it in four words: "International students: Must have UK settled status." A Tunisian national applying from Tunisia cannot take it. This is the most painful loss in the slice — £11,250 for a Falmouth-awarded MA, full-tuition scholarships, no audition, just a video call, an APEL route for non-relevant degrees, and forgiving IELTS sub-scores. Everything about the admissions design suits him except the one thing he cannot change. WaterBear's own stated alternatives are "the 2-year part time online version of the MA Music Business course, or the 1-year online only versions of the MA Songwriting and MA Music Education courses" — all outside production/sound design, all online, none worth pursuing for his goal. Included so he does not spend time on it.

Programme: Zeitabhängige Medien / Sound – Vision (sub-programme of Sound–Vision–Games)

Scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines; Deutschlandstipendium
Accepts non-music?: Yes — explicitly. The accepted-degree list names "computer science, IT (applicants with a degree in applied IT or with a specialism in media are welcome)". Caveat: it requires 210 ECTS, and many 3-year BSc degrees are 180 ECTS — he must check his SMU MedTech credit total.

Entry requirements: Bachelor's degree with at least 210 ECTS in media technology, media systems, computer science, IT (applied IT or media specialism welcome), communication design, illustration or a related subject; German C1; English B1; passed aptitude test.
What you study: Project-centred study at the intersection of science, technology and creative design. Modules cover audio technology and sound design, video technology and image design, VFX production, interactive design, lighting technology and design, plus production and project management. Eight required/elective modules in the chosen branch. Graduates go into audio/video/lighting manufacturers, production studios and theatres. Nationally unique in linking sound, moving image and games.
Facilities: Art and Media Campus Finkenau, Hamburg: audio, video and lighting labs, studios for sound design and interactive media. Facility detail beyond the campus address is UNVERIFIED.
Opens: 1 October (registration for the aptitude test)
Deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: aptitude-test registration 1–31 October (one source says 'until 14 October'); formal application for the study place 1 December–15 January; entry SUMMER semester only, starting early April.
Fit notes: Structurally the friendliest German public option for a software-engineering graduate — CS degrees are named as welcome, the gate is a portfolio not an audition, and the total cost is €397 a semester. Two catches: German C1 (high), and the intake is April only, so a September 2027 start is impossible — he would target April 2027 (apply Oct 2026–Jan 2027) or April 2028. It is also more media/event technology than club-music production.
